The restriction is withdrawn the next time policy is applied, and the capability becomes available to whoever is holding this device.
Confirm
Developer options and USB debugging

Turns off developer options and ADB. USB debugging is the documented way to recover a device whose management app cannot be reached, so switching this on removes the current recovery path. Do not enable it before a signed update has been installed successfully on this hardware.
USB file transfer
The device still charges over USB, but it cannot be mounted as storage, so files cannot be copied on or off with a cable.
Installation from unknown sources
Applications can no longer be installed from a file or from any source outside an approved installer. On Android 10 and later the block also covers other profiles on the device.
All package installation, including stores

Blocks every installer on the device. Android applies this to the management app as well, so Device Guard cannot install its own signed updates while this is on. Leave it off until updates are delivered another way.
Adding and changing accounts
No account can be added, removed or reconfigured in Settings, including an account an installed application needs in order to sign in.
VPN configuration
Whoever is using the device cannot create or edit a VPN. A VPN already configured by management keeps working.
Network settings reset
The Settings action that clears Wi-Fi, mobile data and Bluetooth settings at once becomes unavailable, so management connectivity cannot be dropped by accident.
Tethering and portable hotspot
The device cannot share its connection with other devices over Wi-Fi, USB or Bluetooth.
Wi-Fi network configuration

Whoever is using the device cannot add or change Wi-Fi networks. What a given manufacturer actually refuses varies, so this control is reported on its own and never marks protection as faulty by itself. If the device also loses the network it is managed over, only on-site access can restore it.
Private DNS
The private DNS mode cannot be changed, so name resolution cannot be pointed at an unfiltered resolver. Requires Android 10 or later.
Date, time and time zone
The clock cannot be set by hand. Certificate checks and scheduled tasks depend on it. Requires Android 9 or later.
Safe Boot
The device cannot be restarted into Safe Boot, which would otherwise start it with the management policy inactive.
Factory reset from Settings
The reset action in Settings becomes unavailable. A reset started from the hardware recovery menu is outside what any management application can block.
Additional users and profiles
No new user or work profile can be created, and on Android 9 and later switching users is blocked as well. This prevents a second, unmanaged session on the same device.
Uninstalling applications
Applications cannot be removed from the device by the person using it.
Application controls in Settings
Force stop, clear data and clear cache become unavailable in Settings, so a managed application cannot be neutralised by clearing its state.
Google Play compatibility
Allow applications that need the Google Play Store

Some applications distributed through Google Play refuse to start unless the Play Store package is available, even when Google Play services are working. Turning this on keeps that one package available. Android cannot hide only the Store\'s icon, so on an ordinary launcher the Store may stay visible and can be opened. What is blocked instead is installation: all package installation and installation from unknown sources are enforced and verified for as long as this is on. On a kiosk device the Store is not part of the surface a user can reach. Google Play services and the WebView provider are protected separately and are not changed by this choice. Other application stores stay hidden.
Off — application stores stay hidden
On — the Store package is available and this device confirmed that installation is blocked
On — a maintenance window has opened application-store installation, and it closes with the window
On, but a maintenance window has opened installation from unknown sources, so the Store stays hidden until that window closes
On, but this device has not confirmed the installation lock, so the Store stays hidden
Kept on by Google Play compatibility
Keep the Google Play Store available?

The Google Play Store package stays available to the applications that need it. In exchange, all package installation and installation from unknown sources are switched on, kept on, and read back from the device. Device Guard cannot install its own signed updates while installation is blocked, so plan updates another way before you continue. On an ordinary launcher the Store may remain visible and can be opened; installation is what is blocked. If this device does not confirm the installation lock, the Store is hidden again and protection is reported as not verified.
Hide application stores again?

The Google Play Store package is hidden again the next time policy is applied, and applications that need it may stop starting. The installation controls this mode kept on go back to your own saved choices.
Exemptions from the built-in block
Chrome through the home filter

Only Google Chrome, signed by Google, can be allowed, and only while the home filter is on and protection is active. Before Chrome is shown, Device Guard sets and checks Chrome\'s managed settings: the home filter\'s proxy script is mandatory, so Chrome never connects directly when the script is unavailable; secure DNS, incognito mode, sign-in and developer tools are turned off. These settings also cover Custom Tabs and web apps that open in Chrome. If any condition is not met, Chrome is hidden before anything else changes. Every app\'s traffic still goes through the home filter\'s always-on VPN. Web pages shown inside other apps are not covered by Chrome\'s settings; they are filtered only by the home network. Pausing protection shows every app, Chrome included. Application stores can never be allowed.

Allow Chrome through the home filter?

Chrome will be shown only while the home filter is on and its settings were confirmed in the same check, protection is active, and Android confirms it stored Chrome\'s managed settings, including the mandatory filter proxy. If any condition is not met, Chrome is hidden again automatically. Every other browser stays blocked.

Night and work hours
Suspend apps at night and during work hours

When this is on, every app is suspended from 23:00 to 06:00 every night and from 09:00 to 17:00 Sunday to Thursday, except the phone, messages, clock, home screen and keyboard, essential system apps and the management apps. Suspended apps stay installed and keep their data, but they cannot be opened and their notifications are hidden. The hours follow the time zone this device had when the schedule was turned on. Pausing protection lifts these suspensions.
Off
On
The stored schedule could not be read, so night and work hours are both enforced and protection is reported as not verified
Exact alarms are allowed for Device Guard, so each window is set to start and end at its time.

Exact alarms are not allowed for Device Guard. Android then decides when a window starts or ends, and on a device that is idle or saving battery that can be much later than the set time. To keep windows on time, allow Alarms and reminders for Device Guard in Android Settings.

On this Android version, night and work hours need automatic date and time, so the clock cannot be changed to end a window early. Turning this on asks Android to require automatic date and time; until Android confirms it, the schedule cannot be turned on.
Android did not confirm that automatic date and time is required, so night and work hours stay off.
Turn on night and work hours?
If a window is in progress, apps outside the always-available set are suspended now, and again at the start of every window.
Turn off night and work hours?
Apps the schedule suspended are released now, and no window restricts this device until the schedule is turned on again. The change is recorded in the audit log.
